transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Rachel Li (CTO, MediScape), Priya Nair (DevOps), Ethan Moore (ML Engineer)
Links shared: 1) security package (redwood.com/security) - Samir to share full zip, 2) benchmark plan (sheet link), 3) staging access checklist (short link)

Summary: quick onboarding check-in. Main blockers: VPC peering request / firewall egress, KMS access & key policy questions, and finalizing sample prompt set for tuning. Agreed to run a short benchmark once network access confirmed; Redwood to provide SOC2 + network diagram.

Topics: onboarding progress, access setup (VPC peering / firewall / KMS), environment readiness for benchmark, tuning/batching options, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah this is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Uh Jules our solution eng is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Rachel: Hey Samir, good thanks. We have Priya and Ethan here. Quick morning for us.
[00:12] Priya: morning yep, thanks.
[00:15] Jules: quick agenda — sync on onboarding, confirm network access, KMS questions, runbook for the short benchmark. Should be fast.
[00:24] Ethan: sounds good, yeah we want to get the perf numbers so execs can decide on dedicated vs hosted.
[00:30] Samir: perfect. Starting with onboarding status — Priya, can you run through where infra is on the VPC peering and firewall egress?
[00:38] Priya: sure. So we opened the ticket last week, the peering request is in review — security asked for the network diagram from Redwood which we don't have yet, and a list of IP ranges. Also egress needs an allowlist, we've got a limited window for changes this week.
[00:51] Samir: okay that's expected. I have the high-level diagram in the security package I'll share after the call, it includes IPs and ports. We usually ask for 3.88.12.0/22 (example) and 52.18.x.x range, but I'll include the exact CIDRs.
[01:05] Rachel: also want to confirm encryption — we use a corporate KMS, we need to understand whether Redwood will be able to use our CMKs or we need to use Redwood-managed keys.
[01:14] Jules: short answer: we support either. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account IAM roles, and for Dedicated we have options to support customer-managed keys using an HSM/KMS integration. There may be a policy snippet we'll share.
[01:28] Priya: okay, what's the lead time? Our security wants to see the policy and the exact IAM permissions.
[01:35] Samir: I'll attach the example policy in the security zip. Usually it's a small set of KMS:Encrypt/Decrypt permissions and an AssumeRole trust policy.
[01:43] Ethan: one other infra note — are there any special egress ports for continuous batching or KV cache traffic? Our infra team is paranoid about unknown outbound flows.
[01:53] Jules: no special ports beyond standard HTTPS 443. The KV cache traffic is just normal HTTPS to the service endpoints; nothing crazy like custom ports. We might call out latency-sensitive routes for the dedicated profile.
[02:05] Priya: got it. If everything is 443 that's easier. We still need the FQDNs and IP ranges.
[02:11] Samir: yes, will include full list and staging vs prod differences.
[02:15] Rachel: great. On the POC goals — recap for leadership we had: 1) confirm 99th percentile latency for typical user flows, 2) measure cost per 1k tokens for our seq lengths, 3) verify no data retention issues and KMS integration. Anything to add?
[02:30] Jules: maybe add error behaviour under load — graceful fallbacks, model variant routing. We'll run a short failure mode test in the bench.
[02:38] Ethan: perfect. For the sample workload, our sequences are mostly 128 tokens with a 10% tail up to 1024. I'll drop a small CSV with distribution.
[02:47] Samir: excellent — that helps with batching profile suggestions. On tuning, a few quick notes: smaller batch sizes if you care latency, larger if you care cost. We can recommend a quantization profile for the model you picked to reduce GPU memory and cost.
[03:02] Priya: which model are we testing again? I thought we were on an open Llama variant?
[03:06] Ethan: yes, currently trying llama-3xxq (internal shorthand), but we're open to Redwood's recommended variant if it reduces latency/cost.
[03:13] Jules: for the POC we'd recommend the 7B quantized variant for staging, then if results look good scale to the 13B tuned for dedicated. We can show actual tradeoffs in the bench report.
[03:24] Rachel: what about caching? We have repeated prefixes for some flows, can we use prefix caching or KV cache?
[03:30] Jules: yes, Redwood supports kv cache and prefix caching — small note, the transcript sometimes calls it "kee-vee cache" but it's just the KV cache. You'll see most benefit for repeated prompts; we'll quantify in the bench.
[03:41] Priya: any data leakage concerns with caching? Our security is strict about retaining pii in caches.
[03:47] Jules: caches can be configured to not persist across sessions and can be disabled; for private deployments we can guarantee no persist and in-memory only. We'll document the settings.
[03:56] Ethan: good. For the benchmark, what's our plan?
[04:00] Jules: Plan A: once peering and egress are confirmed, we'll use the staging route. We'll run 1k requests mixed distribution, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and average token cost using Redwood's cost meters. Also include a failure-mode run. Plan B: if network delay is too high, we can run an internal emulation and extrapolate, but pref is staging.
[04:20] Samir: timeline — if Priya can confirm peering by Friday, Jules can kick off bench early next week and deliver results by Tue/Wed.
[04:28] Priya: Friday is tight but we'll try. Security wants the SOC2 docs sooner.
[04:33] Samir: understood, I'll send the SOC2 and ISO summary right after this call. It's the same package we'll attach to the peering request.
[04:41] Rachel: ok thanks. A question on pricing — we want a delta between hosted and dedicated for 50k req/day. Can you give a rough before the bench?
[04:49] Samir: rough ballpark: hosted will be simpler but higher per-token; dedicated gives 30-45% unit cost savings at scale depending on utilization. We'll send a simple TCO sheet with assumptions. Not definitive until we have bench numbers but we can give ranges.
[05:03] Ethan: when you say 30-45% that's at 70% GPU utilization?
[05:07] Samir: roughly yes, that range assumes decent utilization and some quantization. We'll call out the assumptions in the sheet.
[05:14] Priya: security question — do you maintain audit logs for queries and key usage? Our compliance team asks for retention windows and whether logs contain PII.
[05:23] Jules: yes logs are available; we can configure retention and scrub PII from logs. For private deployments logs can stay on customer side. We'll include an audit log section in the package.
[05:34] Rachel: good. Anything blocking the KMS policy exchange?
[05:38] Samir: no — I'll include a sample AssumeRole and KMS policy. If your security wants to do a short readout we can do a separate calls with your security folks next week.
[05:47] Priya: that might help. Also we need a short runbook for what to do if the peering fails — fallbacks.
[05:53] Jules: we have a fallback: route to hosted endpoint with IP allowlist, and we can simulate the dedicated routing locally. We'll document that and include a canary rollout plan.
[06:04] Ethan: awesome. Any other blockers?
[06:07] Priya: one small things — do you require SAML SSO for the initial POC accounts? Our identity team prefers SSO in place before any external access.
[06:15] Samir: not required for the POC; we can create scoped service accounts for the bench. But if you prefer, we can start SSO onboarding in parallel.
[06:23] Rachel: let's do scoped accounts for now to speed the bench, and start SSO in parallel.
[06:28] Samir: sounds good.
[06:31] Jules: quick note on observability — we'll provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency in the bench report so you can map routes to cost.
[06:41] Ethan: great.
[06:43] Samir: ok final recap: Samir will send security package + network diagram today; Priya to confirm peering/egress by 2026-04-03; Ethan to share prompt distribution CSV; Jules to run bench once staging access is confirmed and deliver by 2026-04-07; we'll schedule a follow-up to review the bench and discuss dedicated routing.
[07:02] Rachel: good recap, thanks.
[07:05] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[07:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-ids — speaker labels verified by meeting host, some filler words removed.
